ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: Low-intensity (black/dark grey) pixels account for approximately 75% of the fluke surface, primarily in the central and medial regions, while high-intensity (white/cream) pixels occupy approximately 25% within the distal lateral regions.

The left lobe displays a large, irregular white geometric region with internal low-intensity mottling. The right lobe shows a similar high-intensity cluster at the lateral tip. The central axial region is a solid, continuous low-intensity zone.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: The trailing edge follows a convex curve from the median notch through the mid-lobe, transitioning into a concave sweep toward the distal tips.

localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: A series of distinct, high-contrast linear pixel disruptions (scratches/rake marks) are visible as thin white streaks crossing the low-intensity region of the left lobe.
